newsitem.title: UK: BTPs prosper but gilts falter in week - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: BTPs prosper but gilts falter in week - Salomon.

text.p: Italian BTPs stole a march on other government bond markets in the week to June 19, according to Salomon Brothers World Government Bond Index (WGBI), while British gilts brought up the rear, Salomon Brothers said on Friday.
In total the WGBI showed a loss of 0.25 percent on the week in local currency terms.

During the week European leaders reached agreement over the way forward for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and the details of the stability pact, at the Amsterdam summit. A more certain future for the project sent the Italian market spiralling higher.
BTPs offered investors returns of 0.64 percent in lira terms. In dollar terms they made gains of 0.98 percent, lagging Swedish bonds which offered 1.20 percent returns.
Of the other major European bond markets, France succeeded in making gains of 0.15 percent in local currency terms.
But German Bunds and gilts both failed to offer positive returns. Bunds showed a loss of 0.20 percent, while gilts losses were at 0.65 percent.
U.S. Treasuries and Japanese Government bonds both made positive returns. Treasuries made gains of 0.44 percent and JGBs rose 0.42 percent in yen terms.
Other government bonds within the dollar bloc also fared well, with Canada and Australia offering returns of 0.50 percent and 0.48 percent respectively in local currencies.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
